payload.reason: The evidence explains that higher absolute accuracy numbers compared to F1 scores indicate that human evaluations (which report accuracy) can capture more correct answers than automatic evaluations (which report F1 scores) due to the limitations of the gold answers in automatic evaluations.

claims.text: Higher absolute accuracy numbers than F1 scores suggest that human evaluations can identify more correct answers than automatic evaluations can capture.
The discrepancy arises because automatic evaluations may not account for all possible correct answers in open-ended questions, while human annotators can evaluate correctness more comprehensively.
